name: All Saints
notes: The "cool" alternative to Spice-era pop, and a genuine half-time record: the research gives 67–97 with the backbeat on 3 and a 16th hat on the signature singles, and states that the 134 reading on the 1997 single is a doubled value whose spine is about 67. `halfTime` is true and the snare is `halftime_3`. Three drum deltas are quoted: "heavy kick on 1 and the '&' of 3", "16th hats" with "a shaker and a soft rim ghost" (the shaker/rim perc block plus a real ghost probability), and a kit that is deliberately unshowy, which is the low fill schedule. The bass is the entry's most unusual claim and it is encoded literally — "deep sub with a slow attack, long notes, often a 3rd or 5th rather than the root; almost no movement" — so `followRootsProb` drops to 0.45, the rhythm is `mirror_kick` and the third and fifth are the passing tones. The vocal is "four-part close harmony sung *quietly*; melody conversational and low… note density low, space is the point", which is the low register, the 2–5 density and the pad-leaning counter. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium and says the folding of the doubled readings is inferred. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are all drum probabilities and `bpm.mode` 72. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“deep sub with a slow attack, long notes, often a 3rd or 5th rather than the root; almost no movement.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
